fields.title: What is the value of the gravitational constant G?
fields.text: The gravitational constant G is a fundamental physical constant used to describe the strength of the gravitational force between two masses. It is a key parameter in Newton's law of universal gravitation, which states that every point mass attracts every other point mass by a force acting along the line intersecting both points. The force is proportional to the product of their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them.

fields.title: What is the value of the speed of light in a vacuum?
fields.text: The speed of light in a vacuum is a fundamental physical constant that is denoted by the symbol c. It is approximately equal to 299,792,458 meters per second (m/s) or about 186,282 miles per second (mi/s). The speed of light is a key parameter in the theory of special relativity, which states that the laws of physics are the same for all observers, regardless of their relative motion.

fields.title: What is the value of Planck's constant h?
fields.text: Planck's constant h is a fundamental physical constant that is used to describe the quantization of energy in quantum mechanics. It is denoted by the symbol h and has a value of approximately 6.62607015 x 10^-34 joule seconds (J·s). Planck's constant is a key parameter in the theory of quantum mechanics, which describes the behavior of particles at the atomic and subatomic levels.

fields.title: What is the value of the elementary charge e?
fields.text: The elementary charge e is a fundamental physical constant that is used to describe the charge of a single electron or proton. It is denoted by the symbol e and has a value of approximately 1.602176634 x 10^-19 coulombs (C). The elementary charge is a key parameter in the theory of electromagnetism, which describes the behavior of charged particles and their interactions with electric and magnetic fields.
